observation_summary: The CSS selector parser fails with a SelectorParseException when an attribute regex selector (e.g., [class~=x|y]) is used in combination with other selectors (e.g., div table[class~=x|y]).
hypothesis: The TokenQueue parser logic in the Selector class is incorrectly consuming or failing to handle the pipe character '|' within the attribute regex value, causing the parser to misinterpret the remainder of the query string as an unexpected token.
prediction: The fix will involve updating the TokenQueue or the attribute parsing logic in Selector.java to correctly handle the pipe character within attribute regex values, ensuring the parser does not prematurely terminate or misidentify the token.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points directly to a SelectorParseException thrown by the Selector class when it encounters an unexpected token. Since the failure occurs specifically when using attribute regex selectors in combination, the parsing logic for these attributes is the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the parsing procedure (the algorithm) for CSS selectors. The parser incorrectly identifies the pipe character in the regex as a token boundary or invalid character, leading to a parse exception. This is a procedural logic error in how the query string is tokenized and processed, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition.
evidence_used: org.jsoup.select.Selector$SelectorParseException: Could not parse query '=x|y]': unexpected token at '=x|y]'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a check is failing, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the parsing algorithm for attribute regexes, not just a missing guard.
The issue is internal to the Selector's parsing logic, not a mismatch between two distinct components.
